title: One definition of the Story procedure, stories next, reminders on writes
description:
Ryan 2026-11-03. One definition of how a Story moves through the newsroom, read by the CLI and (later) the context pack. Decisions from Ryan: the outline comes after research; skipped steps WARN and never refuse (publishing stays the only hard gate). No new stages. Human review is never a stage: a person comes in through a review request.

## New module `src/papyrus_content/newsroom_process.py`

Pure data plus pure functions, no model calls.

`STEPS`: an ordered tuple of `Step` (frozen dataclass): `key`, `stage` (a value of `CONTENT_ITEM_STAGES`), `role` (who does it), `title`, `command` (a template with `{story}`), `status` (`live`, `off`, `not_built`), `optional` (bool), `note`.

| key | stage | role | status | done when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| choose | idea | Editor | live | Item.stage is past idea (not idea) |
| direction | assignment | Editor | live | an Assignment on the lineage has a direction in its metadata (`assignment_metadata`) or instructions |
| research | reporting | Reporter | live | any Assignment on the lineage has a research packet (`load_assignment_research_packet_entries`) |
| outline | reporting | Editor agent | live | `Item.metadata.outline` is present |
| draft | copywriting | Copywriter | live | the current version number is above `metadata.outline.versionNumber`; with no outline, the current body is non-empty and the Story stage is copywriting or later |
| fact_check | copywriting | Fact-check agent | not_built (PPY-719a02) | never done yet: returns unknown |
| copy_edit | copywriting | Copywriter with Humanus | live | a finished editorial check run exists for the current version and has no error-level rule violation. Read how `check_after_save` and `reusable_check_run` in `editorial_commands.py`/`editorial_checks.py` store runs; use the existing store, do not add a model |
| editor_review | copywriting | Editor agent | off (`editor_review.tac`, no site has it on) | `metadata.editorReview.versionId` equals the current version id and verdict is approve |
| illustration | illustration | Editor | not_built, optional | unknown |
| typesetting | typesetting | Editor | not_built, optional | unknown |
| publish | published | A person | live | stage is published |

A Step result is `done`, `not_done` or `unknown`. Unknown is honest: never report done without a record.

Functions: `story_facts(client, lineage) -> dict` reads the records once. `assess(facts) -> {"stage", "steps": [{key, title, role, stage, status, state, command, note}], "next": <first step not done whose status is live, else first not done>, "skipped": [...]}`. `skipped` means steps before the Story's current stage that are not done (unknown and not_built steps excluded, optional excluded). Spiked and held Stories have no next step. `assess` is pure over facts so it can be unit tested without a client.

`next_lines(assessment) -> list[str]`: tab-separated CLI lines, same style as the other lines: `next\t<key>\t<role>\t<title>\t<command>`, and `skipped\t<key>\t<title>` for each skipped step. A step that is off or not built says so in the line rather than offering a command.

## New command

`papyrus stories next --story <lineage> [--json]`: read only. Prints each step with its state, then the next lines. Wire it the way `stories show` is wired (see `src/papyrus_content/cli.py` and `story_commands.py`).

## Reminders on writes

After a successful write (never on `--dry-run`), these print `next_lines` to stdout, and with `--json` add `next` to the JSON where the command already prints JSON: `stories create`, `stories move`, `stories save-version`, `stories link-reference`, `stories assign-research`, `assignments research-multi` and `assignments process-proposals` when the Assignment has `itemLineageId`. Best effort: a failure computing the reminder prints one line to stderr and never fails or changes the exit code of a write that succeeded. `stories move` to a later stage prints a warning to stderr naming each skipped step and still moves.

## Outline marker

`papyrus stories save-version --outline`: after saving, write `metadata.outline = {versionId, versionNumber, at, by}` on the new version with an in-place update the way `move_story_stage` writes `stageMoves`. A newer version inherits earlier metadata (read `save_story_version` to confirm), which is why `draft` compares version numbers. Dry run writes nothing.

## Docs

New `docs/story-procedure.md`: the sequence as a table (step, stage, who, command, status), the two decisions above, how to read `stories next`, and that it applies to people and agents alike. Plain prose, no "desk" in prose. A unit test fails when a step key in `STEPS` is missing from the doc's table. Add it to `docs/README.md` and one line to the AGENTS.md map. In `.agents/skills/reporting/SKILL.md` and `.agents/skills/copywriting/SKILL.md`, replace any statement of the sequence with a pointer to `papyrus stories next`; the reporting skill's step "save a first outline draft" goes away (the editor writes the outline, after research). `skills/newsroom-story-cycle/SKILL.md` describes the older edition flow: add one line at the top pointing to `docs/story-procedure.md` for a single Story.

## Specs

`features_backend/story-procedure.feature`, narrative and complete, with steps under `features_backend/steps/`: each step's done and not-done states; next is the first live step not done; a not-built step is unknown and never done; spiked and held have no next; a Story created at copywriting by Create Story shows skipped steps; the reminders print after writes and not on dry runs; a reminder failure does not fail the write; `stories move` warns and still moves; `--outline` records the marker and a later version counts as a draft.

## Done when

Merged to develop by a PR with a merge commit; the feature passes; `procedures/newsroom/tests` related tests and `operator-cli.feature` pass; the guard `procedures/guards/check_pilot_identifiers.py` passes.
